proposals.title: Show the catch volume, not just a ring on the floor
proposals.claim: The tolerance the room enforces is a 0.45 m sphere centred 1.20 m up, but the only thing drawn at that radius is a torus lying on the floor at y=0.015. A visitor aims at the ring, which is directly below the catch and not the catch, so the one number the section is about — how exact the room insists you be — is the one thing the artifact does not show. The stem tethers the arrow to the place; nothing marks the volume.

evidence.quote: Compare two tolerances. A test for whether two points are the same uses a thousandth of a metre, because floating-point equality is unreliable. This room accepts nearly half a metre, because a hand in the air is not a unit test.
The catch is a sphere of radius forty-five centimetres, hanging at chest height where a held bead actually rides.
var centre := global_position + Vector3(0.0, catch_height, 0.0)
_ring.position = Vector3(0.0, 0.015, 0.0)

proposals.build: In _build(), add a faint additive wire sphere of radius catch_radius at Vector3(0, catch_height, 0) — same arrow_color, alpha well under the stem's 0.38, cull_front so it never covers the bead — behind a new `@export var show_catch: bool = true` and a `#show_catch:0` config key in apply_grid_config. Rebuild it with the ring in _rebuild() so a changed catch_radius moves both.

proposals.title: A retention value that keeps the path, not the position
proposals.claim: The section's closing question is about the arc the hand made, and no value of `retention` keeps an arc. `trace` keeps one reading exactly as taken, `archive` keeps seven past positions, `wax` sinks past positions under a sheet — five values, all of them samples. The thing the text says is lost is the trajectory between samples, and the axis has no term for it.

evidence.quote: While you held it, your arm was the instrument writing its coordinates, sampled ninety times a second. The arc, the small correction, the pause before you committed — none of that survives the release.
The switch is here, and it is off, and the arc your hand made is gone. Which of your positions was this room ever willing to keep?
@export var retention: String = "none"
##   trace     one dotted measurement stands after the hand leaves, ending in its marker —

proposals.build: Add `path` to RETENTIONS and to the axis doc block: while held, sample global_position into a local-space polyline at a fixed interval (the existing diagram space, so it stays hand-sized wherever the point stands); on release, commit it as an ImmediateMesh line beside the point, ending in the same marker `trace` uses. Default stays `none`, so the legacy lineage and the 5-value sweep are untouched until a map asks with `#retention:path`.

proposals.title: Let the four arrangements be switched from inside the room
proposals.claim: The section makes its argument by comparing nested against abreast, and a visitor standing in front of the fold can see only nested. `recession` is reachable from a map token and from apply_grid_config and from nowhere else, so the claim the text says you can check in a single still image is exactly the thing the room will not show you. The artifact's own identity block has been asking for this since it was written.

evidence.quote: Four shapes for the past live in that line, and only the first is running.
One thing to carry out of this corner, and you can check it in a single still image: how an object arranges time is a claim, and this one claims containment.
@export_enum("nested", "collapsed", "abreast", "strata") var recession: String = "nested"
# needs: [renders and animates on ready [has], missing a way for the learner to scrub or freeze the fold]

proposals.build: Extract the body of apply_grid_config into `func set_recession(name: String) -> void` (validate through _pick_axis, bail when unchanged, set_process, reset _animation_time, _update_frames) and have apply_grid_config call it. Add the node to a group `ada_folding_past` in _ready and emit `recession_changed(name)`. That makes the axis drivable by anything already in the hall — drag_point_target's `point_arrived` is one line away from stepping it — without changing a single one of the 51 existing placements, which still pass no config.

proposals.title: Print both clocks, so the panel's refusal is visible
proposals.claim: The section turns on the panel knowing when you arrived and not saying so. It does know: _arrival_frame is written in _ready and the captions already carry an 'arrival' wording for every reading. But `epoch` is a choice of one, so a placement shows either the machine's total or yours, never the gap between them — and the gap is the whole point of the paragraph.

evidence.quote: The panel does know when you arrived. It writes the number down, and then declines to use it.
The number on the glass could start from that line. It ships starting from boot.
_arrival_frame = int(Engine.get_process_frames())
@export_enum("boot", "arrival") var epoch: String = "boot"

proposals.build: Add a third epoch value `both`: the big readout keeps the boot figure and the existing prompt line at the screen's bottom-left prints the arrival figure small, with the CAPTIONS entry for 'arrival' as its label. No new geometry — the Prompt Label3D is already built and positioned; it only ever says '> _'. Default stays `boot`, so the 39 placements are untouched; Point_One asks with `#epoch:both`.

proposals.title: The sign's height is the one number a map cannot set
proposals.claim: Every other dimension of this artifact is an export — text, catch_radius, catch_height, colour, and all eight fall parameters — but the label's height is the literal 1.62 added to catch_height, putting the capitals at 2.82 m while the arrow's shaft tops out at 2.32 m. The sign hangs half a metre clear above the assembly it belongs to, and a map that lowers catch_height for a seated hall carries the gap along unchanged.

evidence.quote: A red arrow bobs over a ring on the floor, with a line of capitals under it: DRAG POINT HERE.
_label.position = Vector3(0.0, catch_height + 1.62, 0.0)
shaft.position = Vector3(0.0, catch_height + cone.height + rod.height * 0.5, 0.0)

proposals.build: Add `@export var label_height: float = 1.62` (metres above catch_height) plus a `label_height` key in apply_grid_config, and use it at line 208. Either keep 1.62 as the default and let Point_One tune it, or set the default from the shaft's own top — catch_height + cone.height + rod.height + 0.10 — so the sign sits on the arrow it labels at any catch_height.

proposals.title: Line 60 is the one sentence in the hall that claims a centre
proposals.claim: The comment above the origin variable asserts the centre of the universe; the file's own truth line, twelve lines earlier, says the origin is a convention and not a place. The section is built on that disagreement and can only resolve it one way — the second claim is the testable one. The comment is not documentation of the code, it is a rival argument sitting in the artifact that is supposed to make the other one.

evidence.quote: The comment claims the centre of the universe. The artifact's own truth line, written elsewhere in the same file, says the origin is a convention and not a place.
# The origin - the center of our 3D universe
# truth: the origin is a convention, not a place — but every space must agree on one.

proposals.build: Replace the line-60 comment with the truth line's claim — the agreed zero this space measures from, not its centre — in the same register as the surrounding doc comments. One line, no behaviour, and it stops the artifact contradicting itself in front of a reader who has just been told to ask why that is the middle of anything.

history.title: The hanging sign says "point zero" over a zero the wall no longer measures from
history.claim: The sign is hung at the frame's own origin and reads `point zero`, but `readout_space` now ships as `world`, so the card on the wall reports distances from Vector3.ZERO while the sign directly above the frame's origin still names that spot as the zero — the frame asserts a zero it no longer uses.

evidence.quote: a point is three numbers measured from a zero somebody else agreed on
Place the point, then ask whose zero it answers to.
@export var origin_sign_text: String = "point zero"
@export_enum("world", "local") var readout_space: String = "world"

history.build: In `_add_origin_sign` (lines 166-212), build a second small face line under the caption, the way coordinate_readout builds `_caption` under `_label` (lines 99-107): on `readout_space == "world"`, print this frame's own world position — `frame at 5.0, 0.0, 8.0` — under the sign text, and on `local` print nothing, since local is the only case in which the sign is telling the truth. Gate it behind `@export var origin_sign_space: bool = true` so a map can drop it. The words are already the frame's job (lines 48-52); this makes the sign name whose zero it is, rather than claiming to be the zero.
